title: Sub 4 Hour Marathon Training Plan (16 Weeks)
excerpt: A complete sub-4 marathon schedule in miles and km with exact paces (9:09/mi, 5:41/km). For runners with a ~1:52 half and 25-30 mi (40-48 km) a week.
body:
Sub 4 Hour Marathon Training Plan (16 Weeks)

This sub 4 hour marathon training plan is a 16-week schedule for runners who can already run a half marathon in about 1:52 or faster, and who currently run 25–30 miles (40–48 km) a week. Every session has an exact pace built around the 9:09 per mile (5:41 per km) you need for a 3:59 finish. The full plan is below in miles and kilometres, along with how to adjust it to your fitness.

The plan peaks at 50 miles (80 km) and includes two 20-mile (32 km) long runs. The second has 8 miles at goal pace. Not sure which plan? Compare them here.

Who this plan is for

  • You have run a half marathon in about 1:52 or faster in the last six months, or a 10K in about 51 minutes.
  • You currently run 4–5 days a week, totalling 25–30 miles (40–48 km), with a long run of 10+ miles (16 km).
  • Your goal is specifically to break four hours, and your race is 16 weeks away.

Is your half marathon slower than about 1:55? Then a sub-4 goal is a stretch this cycle. Follow the 16 week plan using a goal pace based on your current fitness, and aim for sub-4 next time.

Sub-4 paces

A 3:59:59 marathon averages 9:09 per mile (5:41 per km). Every session in the plan is set relative to that pace:

  • Easy: 10:10–10:40 /mi (6:19–6:38 /km).
  • Long run: 10:00–10:30 /mi (6:13–6:32 /km), except segments @ MP.
  • MP (goal marathon pace): 9:05–9:09 /mi (5:39–5:41 /km).
  • T (threshold): 8:25–8:40 /mi (5:14–5:23 /km). Jog 2 min between reps.
  • I (intervals): 7:50–8:15 /mi (4:52–5:08 /km). Jog 90 s–2 min between reps.
  • Strides: 20 s quick and relaxed. Walk back to recover.
  • Workout distances include a 1–2 mi (2–3 km) warm-up and cool-down.

The full 16-week sub-4 schedule (miles & km)

The plan runs in three-week cycles: two build weeks followed by one cutback week (weeks 3, 6, 9 and 12). This rhythm gives you more frequent recovery than a four-week cycle, which helps you hit the paces in each session. Tuesday alternates between intervals and threshold runs. Thursday is either a marathon-pace (MP) run or an easy run. Sunday is the long run.

How the 16 weeks are built

  • Weeks 1–6: you start at 30 miles (48 km) and learn goal pace in short blocks of 3–4 miles (5–6 km) on Thursdays. The first long run with an MP finish comes in week 5.
  • Weeks 7–12: Thursday MP runs grow to 6 miles (10 km). Long runs reach 18 and then 20 miles, and weekly mileage reaches 46–47 miles (74–76 km).
  • Week 13: the key session of the plan, a 20-miler with 8 miles (13 km) at 9:09/mile in the second half. Peak week: 50 miles (80 km).
  • Weeks 14–16: taper, at 40, 31 and 14 miles (64, 50 and 23 km). Short MP runs keep the pace familiar.

How to adjust the plan

  • Check-in at week 9: if the 9:09 MP runs feel hard rather than controlled, change your goal to 4:05–4:10 now, not on race day.
  • Heat or hills: run MP sessions by effort on hot or hilly days, and expect your pace to be 10–30 seconds per mile (6–20 s/km) slower.
  • Four days a week: drop the Wednesday easy run. The peak becomes about 43 miles (69 km). You keep every quality session.
  • Kilometres: follow the km values and the per-km paces in the key. They are rounded.
  • Pain or injury: pain that changes how you run, or doesn't ease within a few days, means stop and see a doctor or physio. Don't run through it.

Race-day pacing and fueling

Aim for even splits. Pass halfway in about 1:59–2:00, not faster: going out 2–3 minutes too fast is the most common way to miss sub-4 by a few minutes. In training, practise taking carbohydrate every 30–40 minutes during your MP long runs. Our guide to what a marathon plan should include has fueling targets and a carbohydrate-loading guide.

Related plans

  • 16 week marathon training plan: the same length, with a goal pace you choose.
  • Intermediate marathon training plan: 18 weeks peaking at 55 miles, for faster goals.

FAQ

What pace do I need for a sub 4 hour marathon?

9:09 per mile, or 5:41 per km, on average. On race day, aim for 9:00–9:05 per mile (5:35–5:38 per km) to allow for the extra distance from weaving and corners.

What half marathon time do I need to run a sub-4 marathon?

About 1:52 or faster, run within a few months of the marathon. Multiplying by 2.1 puts a 1:52 half at about 3:55 for a marathon, which gives you a small buffer for a marathon's extra fatigue.

How many miles a week do I need to run for sub-4?

Most runners who break four hours peak at 40–50 miles (64–80 km) a week. This plan peaks at 50 miles (80 km), and its other build weeks range from 30 to 47 miles (48–76 km).

Can I train for a sub-4 marathon running four days a week?

Yes. Drop the Wednesday easy run and keep the rest. If you can only run three days, use our 3 day a week plan with sub-4 paces, though it's a harder way to reach the goal.
keyTakeaway: Sub-4 needs 9:09 per mile (5:41 per km). Train it in short Thursday blocks, then a 20-miler with 8 miles at goal pace, and start the race no faster than goal pace.
